key_insight: Human–LLM collaboration can accelerate materials synthesis by generating and testing candidate recipes, with comparable success rates for humans and LLMs across known and unknown targets.
engineering_relevance: The workflow demonstrates a closed-loop, experiment-driven approach that can reduce trial-and-error in materials discovery and help identify new structural prototypes.
method: Selected the Ruddlesden–Popper homologous series as a testbed for known and potentially undiscovered materials.
Generated synthesis recipes with both humans and LLMs, then validated them through in-lab experimentation.
Fed experimental outcomes back into a closed-loop collaboration to compare performance across rounds.
evidence_signal: Reported success rates showed humans and LLMs performed similarly: 83% vs 75% on known materials in round one, 17% vs 22% on unknown materials in round one, 79% vs 71% on known materials in round two, and 22% vs 14% on unknown materials in round two.
watch_item: Results are promising but limited by a specific materials family and modest success rates for unknown targets, so broader generalization remains unproven.
paper_title: Human and LLM Collaboration for Accelerated Materials Synthesis and Discovery
